findings.body: The Info call is recorded on a brand-new throwaway TestLogger returned by FromContext, so the TestLogger the test holds shows zero Calls/empty Message and log assertions fail or silently pass on nothing.
findings.failure_mode: Tests exercising code paths that log through FromContext can no longer observe emitted logs, undermining verification.
findings.impact: The Info call is recorded on a brand-new throwaway TestLogger returned by FromContext, so the TestLogger the test holds shows zero Calls/empty Message and log assertions fail or silently pass on nothing.
findings.root_cause: The new FromContext implementation constructs a fresh, unshared TestLogger instead of returning a logger that records into the existing Logs fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the same receiver (or one that shares the Logs fields), e.g. `return f`, so log calls made through FromContext are still captured by the test's logger instance.
findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logger state, breaking log assertions
findings.trigger: A test wires the plugins LoggerMiddleware with a *TestLogger and asserts on f.InfoLogs after a request; LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...).
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines R46-48 show FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), a fresh instance. The surrounding source confirms TestLogger stores logs in its own fields (InfoLogs, DebugLogs, etc.). Any test holding a *TestLogger that exercises code calling logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) will not see those logs recorded on the original instance, breaking assertions. The trigger (LoggerMiddleware using FromContext) is realistic per logger_middleware.go context showing m.logger.FromContext pattern.

<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

- Renames the `InstrumentationMiddleware` to `MetricsMiddleware`
- Moves the contextual logger from the `Instrumentation/Metrics middleware` to the `LoggerMiddleware`

**Why do we need this feature?**

Better naming and consistency.

**Who is this feature for?**

Plugins platform.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

<!--

- Automatically closes linked issue when the Pull Request is merged.

Usage: "Fixes #<issue number>", or "Fixes (paste link of issue)"

-->

Fixes #

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
- [x] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [x] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-a-whats-new-document), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/) doc.

raw_findings.body: The Info call is recorded on a brand-new throwaway TestLogger returned by FromContext, so the TestLogger the test holds shows zero Calls/empty Message and log assertions fail or silently pass on nothing.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Tests exercising code paths that log through FromContext can no longer observe emitted logs, undermining verification.
raw_findings.impact: The Info call is recorded on a brand-new throwaway TestLogger returned by FromContext, so the TestLogger the test holds shows zero Calls/empty Message and log assertions fail or silently pass on nothing.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new FromContext implementation constructs a fresh, unshared TestLogger instead of returning a logger that records into the existing Logs fields.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Return the same receiver (or one that shares the Logs fields), e.g. `return f`, so log calls made through FromContext are still captured by the test's logger instance.
raw_findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logger state, breaking log assertions
raw_findings.trigger: A test wires the plugins LoggerMiddleware with a *TestLogger and asserts on f.InfoLogs after a request; LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...).

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the contextual attributes (endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname) injected into the request context would go undetected, since the metrics middleware test no longer covers instrumentContext.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Loss of test coverage for the moved contextual-logging behavior.
raw_findings.impact: Regressions in the contextual attributes (endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname) injected into the request context would go undetected, since the metrics middleware test no longer covers instrumentContext.
raw_findings.root_cause: Behavior relocated from a covered middleware to a new middleware without migrating/adding corresponding tests.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that runs ContextualLoggerMiddleware for each endpoint and asserts the expected contextual attributes are present in the downstream context (e.g., via a fake next client capturing ctx).
raw_findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware added without any test coverage
raw_findings.trigger: The contextual-attribute enrichment behavior was moved out of the (previously tested) instrumentation middleware into this new middleware, but no contextual_logger_middleware_test.go was added.
